1490.etyen:
Borrowed from Latin āmēn (“amen; so be it”), from Koine Greek ᾱ̓μήν (āmḗn, “truly, certainly; so be it”), from Biblical Hebrew אָמֵן (“certainly, truly; amen”). The Hebrew word originally expressed truth or certainty and is related to a Hebrew verb meaning “to strengthen, confirm”. The word is already attested in Old Norwegian around 1200 in the Gammelnorsk homiliebok.
The noun is a nominalization of the interjection.

However, this pronunciation has now established itself more widely, making the current spelling irregular.

en.g: Germany; a country in Europe, in Central Europe, with Berlin as its capital
x: Hun bodde i Tyskland i tre år.
She lived in Germany for three years.
Tyskland er en av Norges viktigste allierte i Europa, og vår viktigste samarbeidspartner i EU.
Germany is one of Norway's most important allies in Europe, and our most important partner in the EU.

1000402.etyen:
From tysk (“German”) + land (“land, country”), literally “German land”. The first element is inherited from Old Norse þýðverskr (“German”) and þýzkr (“German”), from Proto-Germanic *þiudiskaz (“of or relating to a people”), from Proto-Germanic *þeudō (“people, nation”), from Proto-Indo-European *tewtéh₂ (“people”). The second element is inherited from Old Norse land (“land”), from Proto-Germanic *landą (“land”), from Proto-Indo-European *lendʰ- (“land, heath”).
Compare the cognate formations Danish Tyskland, Swedish Tyskland, Faroese Týskland, Icelandic Þýskaland, German Deutschland and Dutch

1000658.etyen: Borrowed from English babysitter. The senses "baby monitor" and "baby bouncer" are a pseudo-anglicism.

en.g: a female given name from Old Norse [in turn from Ancient Greek], an alternative spelling of Karine

1001426.etyen:
A spelling variant of Karine, with initial ⟨C⟩ in place of ⟨K⟩, and a variant of Carina with the ending -ine in place of -ina. Ultimately from Old Norse Kaðrina (“female given name”), a later form of Katrina (“female given name”), from Ancient Greek Αἰκατερίνη (Aikaterínē, “female given name”). The original meaning is uncertain, although the name was associated early with καθαρός (katharós, “pure, chaste”).
Compare Danish Carine, Swedish Carine and French Carine (“female given name”).

en.g: a surname originating as a patronymic, originally meaning “son of Jakob”

1001938.etyen:
From Jakob (“male given name”) + -sen (“patronymic suffix meaning “son of””), originally a patronymic meaning “son of Jakob”.
Compare Danish Jakobsen, Swedish Jakobsson and English Jakobson (“patronymic surnames”).

Last part from Old Norse -ingr m, -ingi m, -ing f, from Proto-Germanic *-ingō, *-ungō.

en.g: a traditional soup from Valdres, made with fresh and/or salted meat, potatoes, root vegetables, and usually peas or barley
x: Denne suppa kalles Majel i Valdres, eller kjøtt og suppe.
This soup is called majel in Valdres, or “meat and soup”.
Vi er kjent for våre gode tradisjonelle valdresretter, som majel (god kjøttsuppe), rakfisk, egenprodusert lam, vilt og fjellørret.
We are known for our good traditional Valdres dishes, such as majel (a good meat soup), rakfisk, our own lamb, game and mountain trout.

1004754.etyen:
A dialectal reduction of matgjerd (“food preparation; meat-and-vegetable soup”), from mat (“food”) + gjerd (“act of making, preparation”). The second element is inherited from Old Norse gerð (“act, action; making”), a nominal derivative of gera (“to do, make”).
The regional spellings majjæl and maiijæl more closely reflect the traditional pronunciation in Hallingdal, while majel is the usual modern written form in Valdres.

en.g: selection felling; periodic felling of selected individual trees or small groups in a forest of varying ages, while maintaining a continuously forested, uneven-aged stand
x: Bledningshogst brukes for å opprettholde en fleraldret og flersjiktet skog.
Selection felling is used to maintain an uneven-aged, multilayered forest.
Ved bledningshogst tar en ut trær i alle sjikt, og gjør ungskogpleie, tynning og foryngelse i ett og samme inngrep.
In selection felling, trees are removed from all layers, and tending, thinning and regeneration are carried out in a single intervention.

1005010.etyen: Compound of bledning (“selection system”) + hogst (“felling, cutting”), with linking -s- (“interfix”), literally “selection-system felling”. The first element is the verbal noun bledning (“selection system”) of ble (“to choose, select; select trees for felling”). hogst (“felling, cutting”) is from Old Norse hǫgstr (“felling, cutting”), related to hǫggva (“to hew, chop”), from Proto-Germanic *hawwaną (“to hew, chop”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kewh₂- (“to hew, strike, forge”).
